_comment: SAMPLE — copy the `permissions.allow` entries below into your OWN settings file.
Nothing reads this file; it is a reference, not configuration.
~/.claude/settings.json          applies to every project you work in — recommended
<project>/.claude/settings.local.json   one project only, and gitignored by convention
Do NOT put it in a repo's tracked .claude/settings.json unless you intend everyone who
clones that repo to inherit your permission decisions.
WHY A BROAD LIST STILL PROMPTS
Agent commands are compound pipelines — `python3 x.py | grep y | sed z`. The whole command
string is evaluated, so ONE unlisted binary anywhere in the chain re-prompts all of it.
`grep` missing from an otherwise complete list is enough to make most commands prompt.
WHAT IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT, and why you should think before adding it
rm, rmdir           destroy work; a prompt is the right friction even when running unattended
curl, wget          reach the network — exfiltration and supply-chain surface
kill, pkill         stop processes you did not start
npm/pip/gem install mutate the toolchain a later step then trusts
chmod, chown        change what is executable
If you want no friction at all, that is a permission MODE (`/permissions`), not an allowlist.
Choose it deliberately rather than reaching it one binary at a time.
